shares_only: D21: every figure is a share of the stock or of estimated need, never an absolute quantity.
undercount_note: The population layer counts about 295,000 people in Landhi against 681,293 in the 2023 census (D16), so the model's estimate of need is roughly 2.3 times too low. Shares of the stock are unaffected by that; any absolute quantity would not be.
water_basis: Sphere Association, The Sphere Handbook: Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Response, 4th edition, Geneva, 2018. Water supply standard 2.1, table "Minimum basic survival water needs" (p. 107), and WASH Appendix 3 (p. 145): survival water intake (drinking and food) is 2.5-3 litres per person per day, depending on climate and individual physiology. 3 L, the top of the range, is used because this is a heatwave. It is a survival figure for drinking only; Sphere's 15 L minimum covers hygiene and cooking too. Verified against the handbook text on 2026-09-27 (P4-02).

scenarios.summary: Drinking water, with stock equal to 25% of the model's estimated need and a 3 km service limit. The plan reaches 57 of 244 areas where people live; the highest-priority fifth of areas receive 26% of the stock. 99 areas are beyond the service limit of every centre that can hold stock and receive nothing. The exact plan and the quick estimate agree to within 0.1%. Illustrative: the allocation settings are provisional (D8) and real need is higher than the model estimates.
